result: {"findings": [{"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 50, "severity": "major", "category": "stability", "title": "The example unwinds past live operations: the queue and its four Async completions die with the coroutine frame", "body": "`go` creates `cq` and `mails` on its coroutine stack and submits all four `Async` operations, but it never closes, cancels or drains the queue. On the non-panic path the defers only cancel the two drivers and the feeder; `go` then returns while the four completions are still pending in the loop, each holding `c.group.owner == &cq` into a stack frame that goes straight back to the stack pool. A late `Async` completion then runs `ownerCallback` on recycled memory: it locks a dead mutex and relinks a dead list. The sibling example cq_spurious_select_repro.zig documents exactly this hazard and guards it with `errdefer { cq.close(); cq.cancelAll(.keep); while (cq.next()) |_| {} }`; this example needs the same teardown inside `go`. The `std.process.exit(0)` at line 75 also skips `defer rt.deinit()` in `main`, so the runtime's own end-of-life assertions (`task_count == 0`, loop deinit) never run and never report the leftover operations. The consequence is worse than a leak: a corruption-induced abort produces the same non-zero exit that the documented harness reads as 'the misuse was detected', so the instrument reports success for the wrong reason."}, {"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 12, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The described death-test harness does not exist, and its stated pass criterion (non-zero exit) does not identify the panic", "body": "The header states 'a harness runs it and checks for a NON-zero exit', but nothing in the repository runs the binary. `build.zig` only adds it to the `examples` step, which compiles it; `check.sh --full` runs only `stderr-smoke`. So the new enforcement this example exists to prove is never exercised by any gate, in CI or locally. Worse, the stated criterion cannot distinguish outcomes: a failed `rt.spawn`, a failed `cq.submit`, a failed `runtime.sleep`, or a crash from the missing teardown all make `main` return an error and exit non-zero, and each would be read as 'the panic fired'. `check.sh` already shows the correct shape a few lines away: it runs `stderr-smoke --panic`, requires a non-zero exit AND greps the output for the exact panic text. Wire this example in the same way and match the string 'CompletionQueue: selected from two tasks; one task must drive the queue'."}, {"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 4, "severity": "minor", "category": "docs", "title": "The panic is not guaranteed: asyncWait's ready fast path never inspects the registration slot", "body": "The header claims 'the second registration finds the queue's registration slot occupied and panics at the point of misuse, in every optimize mode'. `CompletionQueue.asyncWait` (src/completion_queue.zig:398) checks `self.reg != null` only on the not-ready path: when `completed` is non-empty, or the queue is drained, it claims and returns `.ready` without ever looking at `reg`. A single-arm select whose arm is ready returns from the sweep without registering (src/select.zig:329). This example keeps the queue hot on purpose - a feeder that notifies all four mails on every yield - so a scheduling pattern in which each driver always finds a completion waiting lets both drive the queue for the whole 5-second window with no panic. The example then prints 'MISUSE NOT DETECTED: two drivers ran without a panic', which asserts a protocol failure when only the detection window was missed. State the enforcement as best-effort (it fires when the second driver has to park), or make the example force parking - for example, stop the feeder for a stretch so both drivers reach the empty queue."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 1673, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The poison watch reads non-volatile memory, so the optimizer may delete the whole check", "body": "The teardown test poisons `cq` with `@memset(std.mem.asBytes(&cq), 0xAA)` and then reads the bytes back 500 times with plain, non-atomic loads. The compiler is entitled to assume no other thread writes a non-atomic object (a data race is undefined behavior), so it may fold every load to the constant 0xAA and remove the loop, together with the memset. CI runs the suite in ReleaseSafe as well as Debug (check.sh --release, and the `release` matrix leg of .github/workflows/test.yml), so the watch can be dead exactly in the mode where the timing window is narrowest. The test would still pass, and its output would be byte-identical to a real observation. Read through a volatile pointer, or use `@atomicLoad(.monotonic)`, so the loads survive optimization."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 1661, "severity": "minor", "category": "performance", "title": "The new stress tests add 450 runtime rounds to every unit-test run, including the QEMU-emulated CI targets", "body": "The three loops add 50, 200 and 200 rounds to the default suite. The teardown test alone runs, per round, 4 spawned tasks, 64 submitted timers, a full `cancelAll` cancellation storm, and 500 passes over `std.mem.asBytes(&cq)` through `std.testing.expectEqual` - roughly 8 million call-per-byte comparisons across the 200 rounds. The CI job runs `check.sh --full` once per backend inside a single 10-minute timeout (3 backends on most legs), and seven of the matrix legs execute the test binary under `qemu-user`, where both the emulated byte loop and the multi-executor scheduling cost far more than on the host. Reduce the round counts, compare with `std.mem.allEqual`-style bulk checks instead of per-byte `expectEqual`, or gate the heavy rounds behind an environment variable so the default run stays inside the budget."}]}
